what: Real headless Chromium memory for an offline 5v5 match (Jett), before b515533 (index.html at 37c034e) vs after (tip bd76683). Sum over the Chromium process tree (browser process incl. in-process SwiftShader GPU, renderer, utilities, zygotes) from /proc/<pid>/smaps_rollup; RSS double-counts shared pages, PSS does not. Samples taken N seconds after the match was running (frame > 5, loading screen gone).
setup: work/pw daemon (Playwright headless_shell, --use-angle=swiftshader --in-process-gpu --renderer-process-limit=1), viewport 640x360, graphics preset MEDIUM (vs.gq=medium), anti-aliasing off, 2 vCPU / 7.9 GB sandbox shared with the hark-combat soak runs (frame rate 13-18 fps). One run per cell; values fluctuate +-150 MB with GC.
summary: Lotus settled ~2430 -> ~2100-2285 MB RSS (-150 to -330 MB; JS heap 415 -> 290 MB, renderer 1418 -> 1075 MB). Ascent ~3100-3160 -> ~2330-2590 MB RSS (-500 to -830 MB; JS heap 468 -> 290 MB). The browser process (in-process SwiftShader GPU, i.e. the GPU copy held in CPU RAM in this headless setup) did not shrink on Lotus; the savings are page-side (GLTF arrays, decoded images). Much smaller than the modeled map-owned before/after because the browser/GPU copy and the rest of the game (agents, weapons, audio, JS) dominate.
aa_switch: Not established. First attempt (Ascent, tip, MEDIUM, in a running match): Chromium was OOM-killed (browser process anon-rss 3.47 GB, global OOM while the hark-combat soaks ran) during a page.screenshot before the switch; second attempt on Lotus was lost to a sandbox restart.
